title: 3 Money Habits That Build Wealth: Slowly, Then Suddenly
description:
How did you go bankrupt? Two ways: gradually, then suddenly. Wealth works exactly the same way. In this video I break down the 3 money habits behind almost every ordinary millionaire from three angles: the math (savings rate, the crossover point, the cost of a 5-year pause), the psychology of why people quit, and a 30-day setup so the habits run on autopilot.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:35 How we got the numbers
2:02 Slowly, then suddenly
3:05 Angle 1: The Numbers
3:13 Habit 1: Spend less and automate the gap
5:16 Habit 2: Invest consistently and don't interrupt
7:16 The crossover point
8:16 The cost of a pause
9:24 What everyday millionaires have in common
10:42 The habits in a bad decade
11:39 Habit 3: Keep growing what you earn
14:21 Angle 2: The Psychology
19:02 A quick favor
19:14 Angle 3: The Playbook
21:45 Three mistakes that break the habits
22:24 Habit stacking for money
23:27 What a habit looks like in real life
24:24 Ten things you can do today
25:08 Why habits beat a high income
26:03 Three objections
26:58 Three people, three starting points
28:49 What the suddenly feels like
29:47 Questions people ask
32:03 Recap
32:44 What to do next

Sources:
- Ernest Hemingway, The Sun Also Rises (1926): gradually, then suddenly
- Thaler and Benartzi, Save More Tomorrow, Journal of Political Economy (2004)
- Lally et al., How are habits formed, European Journal of Social Psychology (2010): average about 66 days
- BJ Fogg, Tiny Habits (2019); James Clear, Atomic Habits (2018)
- Research on automatic enrollment in retirement plans (Madrian and Shea, 2001)
- IRS, retirement plan contribution and catch-up rules (check current limits)
- Growth and savings rate figures: stated illustrative math (7% nominal; 5% real for independence estimates)
